reviews.text: Pretty good game so far. Good variety of skills to use and has a lot of potential. Would like to see damage meters for the group or some way of seeing damage output potential of your party to help know what are the good skill load outs for them.
I am having fun healing in this single player dungeon experience.
Really good first impressions. It's nice to scratch the itch for healing m+ without resubbing to modern wow.

Loop is very repetitive. The choice of having a time limit in the dungeon seems a really strange choice likely chosen to make the game seem less boring by providing an arbitrary limit to how long you can farm xp. This can be turned off however it seems to be a silly mechanic to begin with (e.g. you get more progression and get stronger by farming a level for all loot. Forcing you to run through only makes you weaker and provides less of a reward even with the 'bonus' that does not change regardless of the size of the map or the difficulty of the enemies). The meta progression unlocks are lame and unappealing (a few percent more health or healing/damage are your only options). The spells you get are broad and highly specific requiring you to semi stragtegise builds and casting rotations, however due to spell upgrades and RNG it quickly becomes so complicated most of the time you just hit buttons and hope things work out. Targeting is terrible meaning you have difficulty determining who you are hitting with you spells. All around just feels extremely janky and poorly thought out. Got boring really quick.

Very interesting concept, as a 20 year vet of world of warcraft alot of this game feels familiar enough to be fun and engaging but without the headache of playing with 4 Romanian gold farmers all trying to ninja every drop that falls.

Absolutely worth the price, very fun. it matches what it is like to be the healer in a MMO game (as someone who has spent decades ALWAYS being the healer on dungeon runs and raid groups). Be warned, it is totally unrealistic in one way and that is the tank doesn't run as far ahead of the healer as possible, pull every mob they can find and then die quickly while you are still trying to reach them, then turning around after you raise them to yell at you for being 'a bad healer'. So in that sense it isn't realistic, but it IS a definite improvement to the reality. 10/10 game for anyone who has ever played as the healer to such a group.

The game is good, but targeting is very frustrating especially when it tries to put in all the healing mechanics known to players currently which includes damaging foes. More user friendliness has to be done to expand the interactable area for hover healing as it's extremely common to lose a run because the wrong target was inexplicably selected.
Healer? I'm dps too!

A game made by people who heal in MMO's. You can tell immediately by the way the UI is arranged and how hover healing is the default etc. I think the game seems fantastic so far. My constructive feedback would be to please give your party the ability to step out of AOE of their own volition. Micromanaging every step they take in battle isn't ideal.

This is a great game, I love the idea behind it, but there are some issues for me. I highly disagree with the design decision, you must micro manage your other party members who are all braindead bots. Babysitting them is very annoying, and takes the fun out of the game for me. Let me just heal them and support them to get through the game that way, just like in a real mmo experience. I'm okay with healing bad teammates to make up for their lack of dodge skills, I'd even say it's realistic. But I'm not okay with being expected to press buttons taking up my hotbar to clunkily navigate them around, while not being able to focus on my healing duties because of that. Please developer, if you're reading this, move the party manager system out of the default gameplay loop. Add it as a challenge or an extra difficulty instead. Maybe something like "raid leader mode" challenge sounds about right.

If you've played a healer in a major MMO, you'll have a pretty good handle on this game. It's a lot of fun at replicating that experience without scheduling issues or griefers. The conceit is that you run through crypts as the healer of a party. At the start of each run you get a selection of healers, tanks, and DPS to make up your party. You need 1 healer, 1 tank, and 3 DPS as is tradition. And every crypt is full of the undead, so your healing spells hurt them if you target them with them, meaning you can be top DPS if you get the right set up. You then try to keep your party alive with vague commands (attack this, go here, follow me), however I have to say they're pretty good at listening to you and are quite responsive to your commands. There are boss fights in the crypts you go into, and lots of them require you to command your party to do something, ie targeting adds, not standing in fire, etc. Through the dungeon you as the healer will level up and get 3 options for either new healing abilities or upgrades to the abilities you have like vampire survivors. A lot of the upgrades are a bit odd as some have downsides that entirely negate the upside. Of course there is a currency you gain in the crypt, and sometimes there are shops. Also there is an optional mechanic to put a time limit on each floor, you get more of the currency the quicker you do the dungeon. You get a whole double hot bar like WoW for putting spells and items into, you also get items which are interesting. You also get skills and armor dropped in the dungeon or from the shop to equip your party with up to 4 skills, and 5 items in various slots for them. They use their skills automatically, so you're not doing that much micromanaging. Your character also has slots for equipment, so putting the right equipment on the right party member is important as equipment has 6 stats, life, phys defence, magic defence, phys damage, magic damage, and crit. After each run you get gold to upgrade your base/characters/unlock new healing spells. It's pretty easy to get what you need for everything except the small incremental upgrades, like 10% phys damage, which is quite expensive. It's a good time, the progression feels sort of weak, but the the game play in the crypts is a lot of fun! The dev really focused on making the game fun before adding addictive meta progression stuff. Overall, a solid 8.5/10 if you used to be an MMO healer or find this idea interesting. The price point is also fantastic.
very good！！！！ It reminds me as a priest in world of warcraft. so cool !

I wish i could recommend this game, because aspects of it are fun but in the end you end up being a raid manager more than a healer. Having to tell my people to not stand in death pools is why i don't want to play an mmo.

This is not a very good game but... its got 26(210+ now) hours out of me. that's pretty good. Note that i add to the bottom here notes at 70 and 200 hours in. what i think the game is about after 200 hours sure you play the healer leader of a party but the dungeons are filled with undead so you are dps too. Your party is just support. only the healer goes up levels and that only brings up an option to take one of three skills. Nothing else is changed. Everything else is gear based. i guess... I kind of equate it to like a fleet and your "healer" is the flagship. there is an option to turn on a dps meter and my healer often has 3x the dps of the other party members. so... a healer but only because the other party members cant heal others. some skills and such will let them heal themselves. there is a slight class system but that is mostly around starting stats, armor type, damage source, and skills, some classes can use multiple sources. but classes are more defined by the equipment and skills. equipment and skills are drops. the healer only gets skills by leveling. there are three armor types light medium heavy. a few damage sources melee(physical), magic, arrows, shields. some "magic spells" are actually physical and does bonus damage based on the physical damage skill. some weapon attacks are magical and need the magic skill to do damage. Or they are a combination. there are many of these classes and they are divided up by healer types/ tanks types/ and dps types. they all can have different or multiple damage sources. the classes themselves aren't random but the availability is randomized. there are a lot of them and you wont be able to choose from them all. so you have to choose your combination from whats available to choose from. this changes at each time you enter a dungeon. there is no carry over and i didnt like that initially. i want my party to keep going. But it works with the game flow and its interesting. i forgot about that fairly quickly. so you are building and engine and you want to pick up skills and equipment to make that engine work. its pretty well done. its different from a standard crawler but not so much that its alienated. its still a party based dungeon crawler. its not turn based its real time. kinda twitchy but im trying to use a build that works with my playstyle and is still effective. i go for insta spells as they are easiest for me to react with. there are no wandering mobs. you attack groups and stationary mobs through the dungeon. They vary in strength and attack types. it works and after a while feels right. --- 20 hours its easy to understand but has some depth in party combination and item bonus stuff like diablo. a dungeon can be finished in an hour or so but i find my self wanting to playing again. what makes it not very good is the lack of polish and content. The content isn't that important. but it doesn't have much. i have barely touched the other two dungeons which you cant get to until you beat the 1st real dungeon. but they kind of seem like the same thing only harder. the polish means things like... i have not found a way to save the game while in a dungeon. there is no next target key that i could find and it can be hard to manually target. have to pay attention a lot. there is not a lot of feedback. i have to tell things to move around occasionally. very occasionally. some bosses that appears a mechanic as part of way to defeat them. trash mobs don't seem to need this much. anyway for 15 bucks... its not bad. i like dungeon crawlers though. particularly party based dungeon crawlers with some positioning in some form. and there are not many of them. edit: i was wrong there are 6 dungeons not including the tutorial dungeon. i have beaten 2 of them. I do not expect that the other dungeons are much different than the first two. still playing it. 70 hours in... its still not a great game. but im still playing it. almost have the last dungeon cleared. i understand the part stuff better. found the dps meter. almost have all bonuses maxed. 200 hours... still haven't beat the final boss. its hard even on unlimited time. its simple game with a deeper level of mastery. getting the right combinations or characters and spells and gear for a wanted "build" still takes about an hour to get through a dungeon which makes it a nice wind down game. i have hit a few bugs but nothing game breaking and they are rare. the primary features all work. its simple but has a depth in party creation and planned build. what item types i want to go for and plan for. It has a fair amount of RNG but not so much that its impossible to plan. that is mostly due to its small amount of content but with the rng its fairly balanced. i can plan for rare items or skills and likely will get them but also possible to have a backup plan and likely will get that. i have gotten both fulfilled. there are spell options that i don't know how to use yet and there may not be a way to use them. i don't know. so while it doesn't have much content there is a lot to master. 200 hours in an i don't have it all figured out. ill get tired of it pretty soon but its a good afterwork time waster but still feels like im learning something about the game. finally. 210 hours. got the last boss. i was not quiet about beating it. i am contemplating playing again. im a little hesitant though. I think buying all the extra spells is not a good idea. I think it increases the rng and i would kinda like to try it by limiting the extra and concentrating on a specific set. i have not beat the game using the 5minute timer. if the game had a little bit more to it it would be better but its functional as it is. it has a "game". a process. Its not too complicated. but it has depth in the combinations and how to get the rng to be less limiting. I think i have the most hours into this game... but its a dungeon crawler and i want a dungeon crawler. its a party based dungeon crawler. It graphics aren't 8 bit or ASCII. it isn't puzzle based. its premise makes sense for the game loop. its repayable. not a great game but it is not terrible. it works. it is complete. there are very noticeable bugs. if it had a squeal or an expansion id play it. if it had more achievements like beating the game with the 5 minute timer or a speed run record that might make me play more.
I wanted to love this game but I cannot get past the first actual dungeon without the game crashing.
Pretty fun experience, but not nearly realistic enough. My tank has not called me a single slur for letting him die during a boss fight.

Was a great game, I would've bought every single expansion to keep playing, but since recently there has been a graphical flickering issue, which unplayable. THUMBS DOWN until game support is provided. SO DISAPPOINTED!

One of the best 5/10s I've played If you were expecting to be able to just sit back and heal and not have to worry about your party's gear, abilities, and especially positioning/targeting... well you'd be dead wrong. It's a hard game that keeps you on your toes, with all the polish and production value of a developer on their 72nd hour of wakefulness trying to cram this student project in before a deadline. But it's pretty fun.
This is a great game for any old school MMO players. It reminds of of play GW1 with the NPC's or multiboxing Everquest with scripts. The rogue lite elements lets you experience many group builds.

The game is fun. It has elements of MMO healing, dungeon crawling and the rouge-lite element adds an extra layer of never knowing exactly what your optimal healing rotation is going to be. Unfortunately, the game crashes constantly. Loading screens are the worst, but sometimes you are just walking down a hallway and boom, run over. It ranges from the game closing suddenly to fully shutting down my machine. It took me 4 attempts to clear the tutorial - and not because I died. It seems to be worse with the damage meter enabled. I am running a brandnew RTX 9070XT and AMD 9700X. I don't know if it's just an issue with newer hardware because my friend that plays on an older PC doesn't have issues. Either way, I cannot recommend a game that I cannot play.

Great idea, but poorly done. I am sorry - it would not have been hard to program the party members with good AI. Them standing in EACH and EVERY AOE, facetanking all damage they can get? This is NOT my idea of fun. I want to heal and fight monsters - not micro manage my party all the time. First dungeon, 2nd Level Boss? Spamming hardcore damage (I am not sure if the AOEs were at all visible or not) and wiping my party 4 times - simply because they facetank EVERYTHING. No chance to outheal that kinda damage at all.

I am so, so disappointed that this game died. It could've been really incredible. As is, it's playable and the gameplay is very fun... But it's straight up abandonware. Very depressing :(( Maybe someday I'll find a game like this one. Maybe. Product received as a gift

Great game, if you played Mini Healer, you will probably like this one, but there are few takes from me: - FPS drop when fighting, it seems like every hit from your bots and monster will drop a lot of frame for that moment, if you have a lot of skills and visual effect, game might crash at some point - No mid game save. This means if you quit or game crash halfway, all your progress is gone, you don't get to save any of the meta progression currency from your playthrough - Monster aggro mechanic is bad. There is no range limitation of aggro, the monster will chase you until you are dead, while hitboxes and bots movespeed are not supporting enough to escape from monster chase, eventually bots that are behind will die. - Solo dev, last update was 5 months ago, updates will be slow mind you. I don't even know if it is abandoned or consider complete at this point.

This game is a great prototype of a really good and interesting game. Full of potential. Unfortunately, it is also woefully unfinished in practically every regard and the last patch was several months ago, so it is probably safe to say that development has been abandoned. A true shame. All of the following would be fixable with more work spent on the game: - The UI is functional, but looks like a first draft. Texts are ludicrously large, placements are kind of random (the UI editor is great, though!), many things (like the store interface) seem to be designed to require twice as many clicks as necessary. It direly needs the hand of someone more experienced in UI design/art. - The game is in dire need of a pause function or better ways to issue commands to units. Or just downright smarter units. Even rudimentary AI like "maybe don't stand in an ongoing DoT area" or "prioritize whatever attacks the healer" would help. But really, what would be needed is a way to set behavior per companion (think ye olden' Dragon Age games). As it is now, everything is just way too frantic and too fast to do anything before it is already too late. - The town upgrades are of the absolute worst kind: A few % increases here and there. Should be done away with entirely and replaced with actually interesting and meaningful upgrades. - The timer in dungeons is pointless. You have no influence over finding or not finding chests fast enough to get the desired map parts for a bonus. It also doesn't make sense: If you find the exit on your own, you get a bonus - if you don't, you advance anyway, automatically and without bonus. ???? I get that the idea is to put some pressure on the player, but there are better and more organic ways to go about that. I could go on with pain points like that, but it feels like wasted effort as I do not believe the game will ever be worked on again.
Good game. Wish it wasn't abandoned and polished a lot more. Due to that I'd recommend getting it on sale.

This is my heavy biased opinion, but I can't express how much I love healing and I really like playing solo. This game hits for me. Needing to direct the party iiiis a bit tedious, but also the party stubbornly standing in the poop is accurate. It fills that healer itch, and keeps me away from mmo's. 10/10

It's a great game, but unfinished, and has since been abandoned by its developer for myriad reasons. I really want to recommend it, but the content that is in the game isn't worth the $15 pricetag. If it's ever on sale or is reduced in price, it's absolutely worth it.

Got this game on sale for 10 and put 13 hours into it in 3 days. If you like WoW healing and want a small but medium depth roguelike then this is your game. Doesn't seem like there are any updates planned but the game is worth its price.

Been looking for a game like this. It's very good. Single player healing/enchanting/dps with a high skill cap. The controls are great. Can easily reposition the team, select target allies and enemies, select enemies you want your team or your team minus your tank to focus. Good variety of spells for PC and NPCs. Has the complexity to keep any player interested, while also being accessible to more casual players I think. Edit: A tip for controlling party. If you want to move them but don't want them bunched together (want them to go back to formation), you can shift 3 then shift 4. As long as enemies aren't too close, they'll go into formation. Would be nice if we could move specific party members instead of all at once, but it works fine.

I wanted to love this game. The core idea is fantastic: an MMO healer simulator where you're the stressed-out healer trying to keep an AI party alive while chaos unfolds around you. That's a genuinely unique concept and one that immediately grabbed my attention. Unfortunately, what exists right now feels less like a finished game and more like several half-finished games competing for attention. The most baffling decision is the complete lack of a save system. In 2026, asking players to commit to lengthy runs without the ability to stop and continue later isn't hardcore design—it's simply hostile to players with jobs, families, responsibilities, or functioning adult schedules. A lack of save functionality is one of those features that instantly changes a game from "I'll keep playing this" to "I'll come back when it's finished." For some players, it's a refund-worthy issue all by itself. Beyond that, the game suffers heavily from feature creep. The healer-focused dungeon gameplay should have been the entire game. That's the hook. That's the interesting part. That's what makes people click the store page. Instead, development effort appears to have been scattered across roguelite systems, town management systems, city-building mechanics, progression systems, and various side activities that all feel underdeveloped rather than complementary. The city-building aspect in particular feels completely disconnected from the experience the game is selling. It comes across less as an essential pillar of the design and more as a side project that wandered into the main game and never left. As a result, none of the systems feel as deep as they should. The healer fantasy isn't fully realized. The AI party management isn't deep enough. The roguelite progression feels thin. The city builder feels shallow. Everything works just enough to show potential, but not enough to feel complete. The frustrating part is that the potential is obvious. There is a genuinely great game hiding in here somewhere. Imagine if every ounce of development effort had gone into making the best possible "MMO healer with AI companions" game: * Smarter party AI. * Better positioning behavior. * More autonomous companions. * More interesting dungeon encounters. * Richer healer gameplay. * More varied party compositions. * Greater tactical depth. Instead of becoming the definitive healer simulator, the game feels like it got distracted by every interesting idea that came along. This doesn't feel like a project that needs more features. It feels like a project that needs ruthless focus. Because underneath all the unfinished systems and conflicting design directions is a game that could be genuinely special.

Don't be put off by the janky graphics, this is a good game! Fun selection of spells and upgrades produce a variety of playstyles. If you find yourself missing MMO healing, or just wanna try something different, it's fun!
Feels a bit like playing an MMO single player at times, but I really like the idea of this game and I think it's one to watch if you like combat which is really number-based efficiency puzzles.

Single-player Rogue-Lite where you play as the Healer. The gameplay is inspired by healing in MMORPGs. Manage a party, Heal your allies, Explore dungeons and Destroy undead monsters.
Support an NPC party as one of 10 healer archetypes in this MMO-style dungeon experience. Beat the timer for bonuses. Gameplay involves use of "Move Here" controls to steer the NPCs out of hazards.
Made with Godot
Play as the healer in a party of your customization, and journey into dungeons to crawl and clear any enemies within your sight. A nice little single player romp.
